<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455dcc060d5c712cc4fbb161b132827a0900e3ac`.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455dcc060d5c712cc4fbb161b132827a0900e3ac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `49eb6add6fa27148f8c9c40fb7932808078ad4ca` — the merge of head `251c5f49b55e33ae92d8bed9745d8e4d6c88be15` into base `455dcc060d5c712cc4fbb161b132827a0900e3ac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 49eb6add6fa27148f8c9c40fb7932808078ad4ca && git checkout 49eb6add6fa27148f8c9c40fb7932808078ad4ca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 455dcc060d5c712cc4fbb161b132827a0900e3ac 251c5f49b55e33ae92d8bed9745d8e4d6c88be15 && git checkout -B drift-repro 455dcc060d5c712cc4fbb161b132827a0900e3ac && git merge --no-ff 251c5f49b55e33ae92d8bed9745d8e4d6c88be15

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455dcc060d5c712cc4fbb161b132827a0900e3ac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 455dcc060d5c712cc4fbb161b132827a0900e3ac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `251c5f49b55e33ae92d8bed9745d8e4d6c88be15`

<sub>Read: card #20003 body and both comments; PR #20180 object, body, 13-file list, full diff (1296 lines), 3 commits, 35 check-runs at the head; at the head via a fetched ref: context-tokens.zod.ts, core filter-tokens.ts and every non-test caller of resolveFilterTokens (engine.ts find/findOne/count/aggregate/update/delete, analytics-service.ts query/generateSql/queryDataset, dataset-executor.ts, read-scope-sql.ts, analytics-date-range.ts), validate-filter-tokens.ts, filter-walk.ts, object-graph.ts recordsOf, authoring-rules.ts registration, page.zod.ts PageTypeSchema and its default, validate-flow-filter-tokens.ts, service-automation template.ts interpolateFilter, error-code-ledger.zod.ts, api-surface and export-origins diffs, the generated mdx, AGENTS.md rule 3 and check-changeset-no-major.mjs. Ran: two Node type-stripped probes over the head sources with a zod stub (resolver: 11 cases; lint rule: 22 cases), vocabulary greps over the eight compile surfaces the PR names, a direct-driver bypass grep, a docblock-vs-mdx fidelity check, and a closing-keyword scan. NOT MEASURED: no package test suite, typecheck, build or ESLint was run here (CI at the head is the evidence); objectui consumers were not read; check:dual-build-cjs-loads and check:type-check-debt (the PR reports them NOT MEASURED locally; CI's four Type Check jobs are green).</sub>

### ① Derived judgments

(a) Vocabulary and classifyFilterToken. A sibling list RECORD_CONTEXT_TOKENS = ['record_id'] with RecordContextToken and isRecordContextToken; CONTEXT_TOKENS is unchanged. classifyFilterToken('{record_id}') and ('${record_id}') return { kind: 'record-context', token: 'record_id' }, a new kind, not 'context' and not 'unknown'. isContextToken('record_id') is false; ContextTokenSchema and ContextTokenPlaceholderSchema still reject it (spec test pins both). isKnownFilterToken('record_id') stays false by design (its one consumer is the flow hand-off, a server position). Near misses {recordid}, {recordId}, {record-id}, {record.id}, {current_record_id} classify 'unknown' with suggestion 'record_id' (the lookup lower-cases the key, so the docblock's "{recordId} ... refused, with {record_id} suggested" holds); '{ record_id }' is 'unknown' with no suggestion; the lit control {current_user_id} classifies 'context' as before. All probe-confirmed at the head. The accept set widens by exactly one token name at the classifier and one kind value on its return union; the changeset names the exhaustive-switch consequence. The module header and the "Deliberately tiny" note are rewritten as the card required for the sibling-list route. Judged: matches card 1.

(b) Server refusal, by name, on every path. resolveFilterToken throws UnresolvedFilterTokenError (name 'UnresolvedFilterTokenError', code 'FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED', status 400, token 'record_id') for a record-context token after the two session branches and before the date-macro switch, whatever the context carries; resolveFilterTokens reaches it because hasFilterToken is true (classify is non-null) and the kind is not 'unknown', so the walk calls resolveFilterToken, which throws. It never returns null, undefined, the literal or an empty tree. Probe at the head: Mongo-shape, operator comparand, ${} spelling, rule-array, nested $and beside a resolvable token, empty context and the direct call all throw that envelope with the message naming {record_id}; the lit control resolves to usr_1. Every server path that receives a filter runs this resolver first: engine find, findOne, count and aggregate via resolveWhereTokens (where) plus the aggregate loop over aggregations[].filter; update and delete via withResolvedWhere (including where.id, before the by-id fast path); analytics query() and generateSql() via resolveQueryTokens (where and each timeDimensions[].dateRange) and resolvedDatasetScopeGetter (scope filter and measureFilters); queryDataset via resolveSelectionTokens (intrinsic filter, measureFilters, runtimeFilter, timeDimensions[].dateRange); the read-scope module re-raises the same throw as READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED / 500 fail-closed with the resolver's by-name message embedded (a server-installed scope, not an authored filter surface; the PR body declares this). Paths that consume a filter without the resolver, each judged: engine having (no token resolution on any verb, pre-existing for every token; having is not a position the card names), formula matchesFilterCondition (0 vocabulary refs, not a server query door), engine execute() (raw SQL/command passthrough, not a filter position), flow interpolateFilter (the flow dialect resolves a bare record_id from its VariableMap; byte-identical because isKnownFilterToken was and is false). No service, runtime, hono, plugin or metadata-protocol file calls a driver's find/count/aggregate/updateMany/deleteMany directly (grep: one comment). analytics-date-range.ts calls resolveFilterToken only with its own fixed date-macro table. Tests: objectql pins find, count, aggregate(where), update(multi), delete(multi) and update(where.id), each asserting name, code, status, token and that the driver method was not called; core pins five filter shapes plus the direct call; analytics pins the direct query door and the dataset executor's runtimeFilter, intrinsic filter and measure filter, each asserting code, status, token and zero captured SQL; lit controls on every suite. Judged: matches card 2 and the Acceptance line for read, write and dataset executor.

(c) Lint rule. pageRecordScope accepts when page.type === 'record' or type is absent (judged as PageSchema's declared default 'record'; the rule is registered input: 'parsed' in authoring-rules.ts, its only registration, so type is always present there, and a test holds the reading equal to PageSchema.parse). Any other type, including null and the wrong-case 'Record', refuses with `no record in context on this surface (a page of type "X")`. The other six surfaces (dashboards, objects, views, reports, datasets, apps) always refuse with their noun. The refusal message contains "no record in context on this surface" and not the unknown-token wording; the near-miss hint on a record page names {record_id} and its scope. The pages collection is walked page by page through the walk's exported scanForFilters with the same recordsOf, the same name-else-id-else-#i label, the same path and where spelling and a fresh seen set (read against filter-walk.ts and pinned by a parity test over an array-shaped and a map-shaped collection). Probe at the head: accepted on a typed record page (Mongo, rule-array with ${}, nested $and beside session tokens and a date macro), in a slotted record page's slot, and on an untyped page; refused, each with the wording and the surface named, on home, app, utility and list pages, a list page's interfaceConfig.filterBy, a top-level view, an object's listViews and a field's lookupFilters, a dashboard widget and globalFilters, a report runtimeFilter, a dataset filter and an app navigation filter; a mixed stack is judged per page; the session tokens stay clean on every refusing surface. Could it wrongly accept on a non-record surface: only an absent type on a raw stack, which by the schema's contract is a record page and which the parsed-only registration never presents. Could it wrongly refuse on a record page: no, every FILTER_KEYS position anywhere beneath a type: 'record' page is accepted. The rule id filter-token-unknown is reused; the message and hint distinguish the two causes; index.ts is untouched. Judged: matches card 3 and the Acceptance line (record-page accept; list view, dashboard widget, non-record page refusals, each tested with the wording).

(d) Public exports. Added to @objectstack/spec/data and regenerated into api-surface/data.json and export-origins/data.json: RECORD_CONTEXT_TOKENS (const), RecordContextToken (type), isRecordContextToken (function), each intended and named in the changeset. Existing exports changed at the type level only: CONTEXT_TOKEN_SUGGESTIONS value type widens to ContextToken | RecordContextToken (named in the changeset), classifyFilterToken's return union gains the record-context member and its suggestion widens (named in the changeset). @objectstack/core adds no export; UnresolvedFilterTokenError gains a record-specific detail message and docblock. @objectstack/lint: index.ts untouched, FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN unchanged, the new TokenFilterSurface and RecordScope are module-private. filter-walk.ts and engine.ts are untouched, as the claim required. No unintended export changed.

(e) Envelope. The refusal is UnresolvedFilterTokenError with status 400 and code FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED, the ADR-0112 shape the REST passthrough maps; the code already sits in error-code-ledger.zod.ts under @objectstack/core (line 848), so no ledger row was owed and the reuse follows the existing member's definition (a vocabulary token the request carries no value for; token names which context). The core and lint messages carry no tracker number (probe: msgHasTrackerNo false on every throw; lint tracker false on every finding). The refusal tests assert code and status on every suite (core, objectql, service-analytics), plus token and, in objectql, name. The PR's per-compile-surface list holds: driver-sql sql-driver.ts, turso remote-transport.ts, driver-memory memory-matcher.ts, driver-mongodb mongodb-filter.ts, formula matches-filter.ts, objectql having-filter.ts and analytics filter-normalizer.ts each have 0 vocabulary references; read-scope-sql.ts has the 2 wrapper references it declares. The generated context-tokens.mdx contains all 121 docblock lines and 5 headings of the module header.

### ② Semver level

.changeset/20003-record-id-filter-token.md grades @objectstack/spec, @objectstack/core and @objectstack/lint each minor; objectql and service-analytics move test files only and owe no changeset. Its prose names where the token is accepted (any filter on a component of a type: 'record' page, regions, slots, the untyped default) and where it is refused (lint: views, object list views and field filters, dashboard widgets and filters, reports, datasets, app navigation, every non-record page type including a list page's filterBy; server: every ObjectQL read and write verb, the analytics query door and the dataset executor, with the FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED / 400 envelope), as card 5 requires. The PR body's Clause-②: yes matches the diff: three new keys on a published payload plus a new kind value, and at least one touched package graded minor (AGENTS.md rule 3: yes takes at least minor; the widening arm is optional and no ADR-0087 marker is owed by a non-breaking changeset). Check Changeset is green at the head. Judged: correct levels, correct declaration.

### ③ Boundary flags
Blocking: none
Non-blocking: (1) validate-flow-filter-tokens.ts's early-return comment names context and date-macro only while record-context now also returns early; behaviour is unchanged (a bare record_id was an open-oracle identifier the second layer already passed silently), outside the claimed surface, carrier none. (2) The published skills teach only the session tokens; teaching {record_id} before a renderer resolves it would steer authors into the server refusal; Tier H, carrier objectui#7297's landing. (3) authoring-rule-command-parity (CLI integration project) was not run locally by the author; Dogfood Verify CLI and the Test Core shards are green at the head. (4) The read-scope path re-raises as READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED / 500 rather than 400: the module's pre-existing fail-closed contract for any placeholder in a server-installed scope, not an authored filter surface, and declared in the PR body. (5) having is not a token position on any verb, pre-existing for every token; the card names read, write and the dataset executor, not having. (6) findOne, delete by where.id, aggregations[].filter and generateSql have no {record_id} pin of their own; each shares the exact seam a pinned verb uses (resolveWhereTokens, withResolvedWhere, the aggregate loop, resolveQueryTokens). (7) The branch was 2 commits behind main at report time on disjoint files; mergeable_state is clean. (8) isKnownFilterToken('record_id') stays false, so a {record_id} in a flow node filter follows the flow's own unresolved-variable path rather than a hand-off; deliberate, documented in the spec docblock and the changeset. The PR's "Not in this PR" items (the objectui resolver, other tokens, RLS current_user.*, AppContextSelector ids, titleFormat) match the card's Out of scope list exactly.

CI at this head: 35 check-runs, 35 unique names after de-duplication on latest started_at: 33 success, 2 skipped (Console Pin Gate; Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Closing keywords: only `Fixes #20003`; `#20148` and objectui `#7297` appear as plain mentions in the body, and no commit message carries an issue reference.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20003-record-id-filter-token`
Reviewed-by: `session_01CiCTczDo7tGhafXjf61dUJ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
